description: This package contains MCP tools for image generation. So Fuuga (or other agents) can gain image generation capabilities via other (Stable Diffusion) models from for example HuggingFace.
releaseNotes: Version aligned with Fuuga 1.0.31. RESOURCE FIXES: scratch SD generation frees its text conditioning and, on error, its latents; scratch weight loading no longer leaves a flat copy of every tensor to the finalizer; a failed scratch load or caption-processor creation disposes its models; scratch export frees its per-tensor CPU copies; the MCP server disposes its parsed request documents. PREVIOUS (1.0.30) - Version aligned with Fuuga 1.0.30; no Fuuga.Image changes. PREVIOUS (1.0.29) - New Fuuga.Image.cuda-linux package: the CUDA 12.8 natives for Linux x64 (libtorch, stable-diffusion.cpp CUDA backend, ONNX Runtime GenAI CUDA), built with -p:TorchBackend=cuda-linux; Fuuga.Image stays the Windows x64 CUDA build and Fuuga.Image.cpu runs anywhere. Diffusion.loadModel now says in a sentence when the stable-diffusion.cpp backend cannot run here - Apple Silicon and other Arm machines have no natives (and no Metal backend exists), and a native load failure names the package and what it needs - instead of surfacing the loader's exception (new Diffusion.backendUnavailableReason / describeNativeLoadFailure). Otherwise version alignment with Fuuga 1.0.29. PREVIOUS (1.0.28) - DEPENDENCY UPDATES, no functional changes: Microsoft.ML.OnnxRuntimeGenAI 0.17.1 (captioning runtime; the CUDA package likewise). PREVIOUS (1.0.27) — version alignment with Fuuga 1.0.27 (donor imports: latent attention and encoder donors). No functional changes in Fuuga.Image. PREVIOUS (1.0.26) — robustness fixes. One change in Fuuga.Image: generated file names and temp files are stamped with UTC ticks instead of local-clock ticks, because the local clock repeats an hour when daylight saving ends and a stamp from that hour can reproduce an earlier file name. The name format is unchanged. PREVIOUS (1.0.19) — PERFORMANCE: MCP server mode keeps the most recently used diffusion and caption models resident between tool calls — previously every tool call paid a full model load (the dominant fixed cost of a generation) because the dispatcher re-entered the one-shot CLI paths; models reload only when the model path or its options change. Weights are no longer force-re-quantized to Q5_1 on load: the default is now `native` (keep the weight file's own type), which loads faster and stops silently changing quality; pass --quantization to opt into a conversion, and img2img finally accepts --quantization at all. --batch N is now implemented rather than parsed-and-discarded: N candidate images generate on ONE model load, each with a distinct reported seed, enabling a preview-then-refine flow (--batch 4 --steps 12, pick the best, re-run its --seed with full steps — generation is seed-deterministic). The MCP txt2img tool exposes the same via a `batch` argument. All diffusion commands accept --threads (physical-core count is usually fastest for stable-diffusion.cpp). Model load time is now reported ("Model ready in Nms") — it was previously invisible next to generation time. Dependencies: Microsoft.ML.OnnxRuntimeGenAI 0.15.0 (captioning runtime), FSharp.Core 10.1.302.
